In scope are open quotes whose expiry date falls within the next 14 days or has already passed as at the run date; effective window = run date to run date + 14 days plus past-due.

checklist.step: Monitor quotes against the firm-quote SLA window
checklist.value: The diary surfaces quotes approaching expiry so re-quote or follow-up happens within SLA rather than after lapse.

checklist.step: Assign an owner to at-risk quotes
checklist.value: Each at-risk diary entry has a named owner responsible for the next action.

testing.value: For a sampled run, 100% of quotes within 14 days of expiry or past due are flagged; misses fail.
Sampled at-risk entries each have an assigned owner; unowned entries fail.

checklist.value: Each diary run is saved with parameters and timestamp so the at-risk population is auditable.

checklist.step: Reconcile the diary to open quotes
checklist.value: The diary is reconciled to the PolicyCenter open-quote inventory so nothing falls off the radar.

testing.value: Sampled diary runs have retained parameters, counts and timestamp; missing evidence fails.
Diary open-quote count equals the PolicyCenter open-quote report; variance is investigated.

answers.value: Re-priced quotes whose terms deviate materially from the original quote and therefore require referral approval before issue; scope is the quotes in this cycle whose deviation exceeds the underwriter's authority.
The current re-pricing cycle (e.g. week ending 2026-06-27); approval must be on file before the revised quote is issued in that window.

The referral shows the original vs re-priced terms, the deviation size, the triggering threshold, the underwriter's recommendation and the approver's decision; a referral missing the deviation size or the decision is not complete.

The deviation size stated in the referral reconciles to the difference between original and re-priced premium/terms in Earnix; every quote flagged as material deviation has a matching referral record, with 0 unreferred material deviations issued.
The referral request and the approval decision are recorded on the quote in PolicyCenter and stored in OpenText /uw/quotes/<quote-id>/referrals/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.

A material deviation issued without approval is a control breach: it is logged, escalated to the Chief Underwriting Officer, and the quote is withdrawn/reissued only after approval; the exception is recorded with disposition.
Materiality thresholds and referral triggers come from the approved Underwriting Authority Matrix v3.2 (premium, limit and filed-rate deviation bands).
A deviation exceeding +/-15% of filed premium, or any change breaching the authority band, is treated as material and requires referral.
Deviations at or above the CUO tier of the authority matrix require Chief Underwriting Officer approval; lower tiers require Senior Underwriter approval.
All re-priced quotes in the cycle flagged as material deviations (census of referral-triggering quotes).

PASS = every material-deviation quote has a referral approval at the correct authority tier on file before issue; FAIL = any material deviation issued without approval or approved below the required tier.
Where approval is declined, the quote is re-worked within authority or withdrawn; unresolved referrals hold the quote and escalate to the CUO.
Acceptance = a documented approval at the authority tier required by the matrix is on file for every material deviation before the revised quote is issued.
Evidence (referral request and approval decision) lands on the quote in PolicyCenter and OpenText /uw/quotes/<quote-id>/referrals/.

Material/tolerance thresholds are set by the Underwriting Authority Matrix v3.2: filed-premium deviation beyond +/-15% or any breach of the underwriter's premium/limit authority band triggers referral, with the approval tier (Senior Underwriter vs CUO) set by the band.

checklist.value: The re-priced quote is tested against the documented referral triggers (deviation %, premium/limit bands) in the authority matrix.
Where a trigger is hit, a referral is raised before issue rather than the underwriter proceeding on own authority.

testing.value: Sampled material-deviation quotes show the trigger that fired; unraised referrals on triggered quotes fail.
0 quotes issued past the underwriter's authority without a referral.

checklist.step: Refer to the next authority level with a recommendation
checklist.value: The referral routes to the correct next authority (Senior Underwriter or CUO) with the underwriter's recommendation attached.
The approver's decision and any conditions are recorded on the referral before the quote proceeds.

testing.value: Sampled referrals were approved at the tier required by the deviation band; under-tier approvals fail.
100% of sampled referrals include the underwriter recommendation and a recorded decision.

checklist.step: Require CUO approval with documentation for top-tier exceptions
checklist.value: Deviations at the CUO tier are approved by the Chief Underwriting Officer with documented rationale on file.
The exception/approval is stored on the quote so authority usage is auditable.

testing.value: Sampled top-tier deviations show CUO approval with documentation; missing sign-off fails.
Each sampled top-tier exception is retained with rationale in OpenText; 0 gaps.
